chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayn, who said:

I said to him, 'The wife of Abd al-Malik gave birth, so he counted for her the days of her menstruation, then he ordered her to perform ghusl and insert a cloth (for istihada), and he ordered her to wear two clean garments, and he ordered her to perform salat. She said to him, 'I do not feel comfortable entering the mosque, so let me stand outside of it and prostrate within it.'

He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had ordered with it, and said: When the blood ceases from the woman and she sees purity.' And Ali (peace be upon him) had ordered with this before you: 'When the blood ceases from the woman and she sees purity.' So what did your companion do? I said, 'I do not know.'

key_terms.صَاحِبَتُكُمْ: Your companion (referring to the wife of Abd al-Malik)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who continues to bleed after childbirth and how should she perform prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between post-childbirth bleeding (nafsāʾ) and irregular bleeding (istihāḍah), establishing that the cessation of blood flow, rather than a fixed duration, triggers the obligation of ghusl and resumption of prayer. It highlights the practical flexibility granted to women, allowing them to pray outside the mosque if they feel unclean, while affirming the continuity of this ruling from the Prophet and Imam Ali (peace be upon him). The narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on observable purity signs over rigid temporal limits in personal status law.
